# STAGE 1 of 2 — time-averaged steady-state calibration

Calibrates the 18/19-species ESS size-spectrum model to the **1978-85 reference
period** (high groundfish, low pelagics). Output `params_stage1_steady.RDS` feeds
**Stage 2** (`02_Calibration_Stage2_AUTO.R`), which projects through the
historical effort and tunes the dynamic processes (collapse + non-recovery).

Corrections incorporated (see ESS_calibration_status.md):
- **Empirical seal gear** (`seal_gear_params.csv`, Bowen & Harrison 1994): per-species
  w_opt = mean prey weights (15-201 g), sigma 0.75 — replaces the flat 1500 g placeholder.
- **Lower cutoff = abundance-weighted q05 length** (the size below which only ~5% of
  caught individuals fall) — replaces the occurrence-floor cutoff that put the gadoid
  cutoffs at 4-6 cm and crashed the within-window mean-weight indicator on recruit pulses.
- **biomass_cutoffHigh = biomass-weighted q99** (upper *reporting* cutoff; not used in matchBiomasses).
- **w_max = biomass-weighted q99.9 survey length** (regional max size), replacing the FishBase record
  Lmax that over-inflated the largest species (cod 198->136 cm, halibut 484->206 cm) and drove an
  unrealistic giant-fish pile-up at w_max once recruitment collapses in Stage 2. Herring held at its
  FishBase value (small forage species, not subject to the pile-up).

Diagnostics at the end: size spectra, growth curves, biomass/yield fits, emergent
diet heatmap vs Cook & Bundy (2010), and seal "catch" composition vs Bowen & Harrison (1994).

```{r}
species_lookup <- c(

  "Melanogrammus aeglefinus"       = "Haddock",

  "Urophycis chuss"                = "Red Hake",
  "Merluccius bilinearis"          = "Silver Hake",
  "Pollachius virens"              = "Pollock",
  "Sebastes fasciatus"             = "Redfish Unseparated",
  "Hippoglossoides platessoides"   = "American Plaice",
  "Myzopsetta ferruginea"          = "Yellowtail Flounder",  ## Limanda ferruginea
  "Glyptocephalus cynoglossus"     = "Witch Flounder", 
  "Clupea harengus"                = "Atlantic Herring",
  "Mallotus villosus"              = "Capelin",
  "Amblyraja radiata"              = "Thorny Skate",
  "Leucoraja ocellata"             = "Winter Skate", 
  "Squalus acanthias"              = "Spiny Dogfish", 
  "Lophius americanus"             = "Monkfish",  
  "Ammodytes dubius"               = "Sand Lance",
  "Myoxocephalus octodecemspinosus" = "Longhorn Sculpin",
  "Hippoglossus hippoglossus"      = "Atlantic Halibut")

species_order <- c( "Atlantic Cod", "Haddock", "White Hake", "Red Hake", "Silver Hake",
                    "Pollock", "Redfish Unseparated","American Plaice", "Yellowtail Flounder",
                    "Witch Flounder", "Atlantic Herring","Capelin", "Thorny Skate", 
                    "Winter Skate", "Spiny Dogfish", "Monkfish", "Sand Lance",
                    "Longhorn Sculpin",  "Atlantic Halibut")

external_species_info <- read.csv("Ess_data/ESS_species_params.csv") |>
 #Hartvig et al. 2011 ; preferred (roughly) should be realised ppmr divided by 2
# I think min_ppmr_adj or min_ppmr probably best reflection of "preferred" ppmr; else could use a box predation kernel
 select(-beta) |>
  rename(beta = min_ppmr_adj) |>
  select(Species, w_max, w_mat, w_min, l_mat, beta, sigma, k_vb, a, b, age_mat) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3)),
  Species = factor(recode(Species, !!!species_lookup), levels = species_order)) |>

years_to_use<-as.character(1978:1981)  # Reference (base) period for the steady state: the relatively STABLE post-EEZ plateau selected by a rolling-window stability screen (see below). 1978-81 has CV=0.12 and ~zero trend in cod survey biomass; the early-1970s foreign-fleet era is erratic (CV 0.7-0.9) and 1982-83 is a transient spike (CV>0.5), so both are excluded.

# #The initial Rmax was estimated from an empirical equation as in (Blanchard et al., 2014)
external_species_info <- external_species_info |> mutate(R_max = 10^13 * w_max^-1.5)
```

Read in DFO Summer RV survey abundance and biomass data from DFO Maritimes region data team, subset depth strata to include only 4VsW (in line with Bundy et al. EwE spatial domain).

Calculate the minimum length and weight cutoffs from length distributions for us in model, to account for the fact that smaller sizes not selected by the RV gear. Maybe should add a maximum length and weight as well.
```{r}
stat <- read.csv("Ess_data/LF_Biomass_Abund.csv")

# ── LOOKUP: RAW SURVEY NAME -> MODEL NAME ────────────────────────────────────
species_code_lookup <- c(
  "COD(ATLANTIC)"             = "Atlantic Cod",
  "HADDOCK"                   = "Haddock",
  "WHITE HAKE"                = "White Hake",
  "SILVER HAKE"               = "Silver Hake",
  "POLLOCK"                   = "Pollock",
  "REDFISH UNSEPARATED"       = "Redfish Unseparated",
  "AMERICAN PLAICE"           = "American Plaice",
  "YELLOWTAIL FLOUNDER"       = "Yellowtail Flounder",
  "SPINY DOGFISH"             = "Spiny Dogfish",
  "HALIBUT(ATLANTIC)"         = "Atlantic Halibut",
  "SQUIRREL OR RED HAKE"      = "Red Hake",
  "MONKFISH,GOOSEFISH,ANGLER" = "Monkfish",
  "NORTHERN SAND LANCE"       = "Sand Lance",
  "WITCH FLOUNDER"            = "Witch Flounder",
  "HERRING(ATLANTIC)"         = "Atlantic Herring",
  "THORNY SKATE"              = "Thorny Skate",
  "WINTER SKATE"              = "Winter Skate",
  "LONGHORN SCULPIN"          = "Longhorn Sculpin",
  "CAPELIN"                   = "Capelin")


# Species lookup
stat2 <- stat |>
  filter(YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 2024) |>
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) |>
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466) |>  # 4VsW only
  select(
    depth_strata = STRAT,
    year = YEAR,
    species_name_raw = COMMON_NAME,
    length_cm = FLEN,
    abundance = Abundance_Strata) |>
  mutate(
    length_cm = ifelse(
      species_name_raw == "HERRING(ATLANTIC)", # herring looks like measured in mm!
      length_cm / 10,
      length_cm),
    species_name = species_code_lookup[species_name_raw]) |>
  filter(!is.na(species_name))

# 1. Sum abundance across depth strata by species, year and length
lf_year_length <- stat2 %>%
  group_by(species_name, year, length_cm) %>%
  summarise(
    abundance = sum(abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

# ── LOWER GEAR-RETENTION CUTOFF (abundance-weighted q05 length) ──────────────
# The lower cutoff is computed below as the abundance-weighted 5th-percentile of
# length (see `lower_cutoff`, after weighted_quantile is defined). Rationale and
# derivation are documented there.


weighted_quantile <- function(x, w, probs = 0.05) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
  x <- x[ok]
  w <- w[ok]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)

  o <- order(x)
  x <- x[o]
  w <- w[o]

  cw <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  x[which(cw >= probs)[1]]
}

# ── LOWER GEAR-RETENTION CUTOFF = abundance-weighted 5th-percentile length ────
# The survey trawl under-catches small fish, so the lower cutoff marks where the
# gear starts reliably retaining a species: the length below which only ~5% of the
# individuals it catches (by number) fall. Computed as the abundance-weighted 5th
# percentile of length, POOLED across all survey years (robust — a single odd tow
# cannot move a q05). This REPLACES the earlier occurrence-floor cutoff, whose
# "caught in >= 1/3 of years" floor picked up rare larval/juvenile bins and put the
# gadoid cutoffs at 4-6 cm (e.g. cod 6 cm / 1.7 g). That artificially low cutoff let
# occasional recruit pulses dominate the within-window mean-weight indicator (04),
# collapsing it (cod 2024 mean weight -> 55 g vs a survey ~1 kg). The q05 gives
# realistic, gear-appropriate cutoffs (cod 18 cm / 51 g, silver hake 23 g,
# white hake 118 g, pollock 194 g).
lower_cutoff <- lf_year_length %>%
  group_by(species_name) %>%
  summarise(lower_cm = weighted_quantile(length_cm, abundance, 0.05),
            .groups = "drop")

lower_cutoff

# Overall length distributions for display, BIOMASS-weighted (shows where the biomass
# sits and the size range carrying the biomass-weighted UPPER cutoff). NB: the dashed
# LOWER cutoff overlaid below is the abundance-weighted q05 length (a count-based
# gear-retention threshold), so it sits at the small end where the biomass is low.
lf_overall <- lf_year_length %>%
  left_join(external_species_info %>% select(species, a, b),
            by = c("species_name" = "species")) %>%
  mutate(
    length_bin = floor(length_cm / 2) * 2,
    biomass    = abundance * a * length_cm ^ b
  ) %>%
  group_by(species_name, length_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    biomass = sum(biomass, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_name), !is.na(length_bin), biomass > 0)

# Lower size cutoff (abundance-weighted q05 length — gear retention)
length_thresholds <- lower_cutoff %>%
  transmute(
    species_name,
    threshold_cm = lower_cm)



# Plot (biomass-weighted)
ggplot(lf_overall, aes(x = length_bin, y = biomass)) +
  geom_col(width = 1.8) +
  geom_vline(
    data = length_thresholds,
    aes(xintercept = threshold_cm),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6 ) +
  facet_wrap(~species_name, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Length (cm)",
    y = "Total stratified biomass (g)",
    title = "Biomass-weighted length distributions across all years and strata",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = lower size cutoff (abundance-weighted 5th-percentile length)")



# ── LOWER SIZE CUTOFF FOR ESTIMATING BIOMASS (abundance-weighted q05 length) ──
# = weight at the abundance-weighted 5th-percentile length (the size below which
#   only ~5% of caught individuals fall — where the gear starts retaining the fish).
# matchBiomasses then compares model biomass ABOVE this cutoff to the survey total
# (which itself only ever contains fish above gear retention) — i.e. both sides are
# on the SAME, comparable size range, and mizer estimates the unsampled small end
# self-consistently.
biomass_cutoff <- lower_cutoff |>
  left_join(
    external_species_info |>
      select(species, a, b),
    by = c("species_name" = "species")) |>
  mutate(
    biomass_cutoff = round(a * lower_cm ^ b, 1)) |>
  select(
    species = species_name,
    biomass_cutoff)

# ── JOIN BACK TO SPECIES INFO ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Drop any pre-existing cutoff cols first so re-running THIS chunk alone (without
# re-reading external_species_info) doesn't create biomass_cutoff.x/.y duplicates.
external_species_info <- external_species_info |>
  select(-any_of("biomass_cutoff")) |>
  left_join(
    biomass_cutoff,
    by = "species")


# ── SURVEY-DERIVED UPPER REPORTING CUTOFF AND MAX SIZE (w_max override) ───────
# From the BIOMASS-weighted length distribution the survey actually catches:
#   biomass_cutoffHigh = biomass-weighted q99   -> UPPER REPORTING cutoff (used in 04
#                        and for display; NOT in matchBiomasses, which uses only the
#                        lower cutoff against the survey total).
#   w_max (override)   = biomass-weighted q99.9 -> regional MAX SIZE (see override below).
# Biomass-weighting (not abundance) makes the quantiles reflect the size range carrying
# the biomass, not the numerous juveniles (corrected 2026-06: was abundance-weighted,
# which put the cutoff far below the large fish actually caught).
survey_max_lengths <- stat2 %>%
  left_join(external_species_info %>% select(species, a, b),
            by = c("species_name" = "species")) %>%
  mutate(biomass_at_length = abundance * a * length_cm ^ b) %>%
  group_by(species_name) %>%
  summarise(
    survey_max_length_cm = max(length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
    q99_length_cm  = weighted_quantile(length_cm, biomass_at_length, 0.99),
    q999_length_cm = weighted_quantile(length_cm, biomass_at_length, 0.999),
    .groups = "drop")

# Convert survey lengths to weights using W = aL^b.
max_weight_comparison <- survey_max_lengths %>%
  left_join(
    external_species_info %>% select(species, a, b, w_max),
    by = c("species_name" = "species")) %>%
  mutate(
    survey_max_weight_g = a * survey_max_length_cm ^ b,
    biomass_cutoffHigh  = a * q99_length_cm ^ b,   # q99  -> reporting cutoff
    w_max_survey        = a * q999_length_cm ^ b,  # q99.9 -> regional max size
    old_wmax_ratio      = w_max / w_max_survey      # FishBase-record w_max as a multiple of survey q99.9
  )                                                 #   (>~2 flags an over-inflated FishBase Lmax)

max_weight_comparison

# ── OVERRIDE w_max WITH THE SURVEY-DERIVED REGIONAL MAX SIZE ──────────────────
# mizer 2.5.x defines w_max as the species' maximum size (the von-Bertalanffy w_inf
# route is deprecated). FishBase's *global record* Lmax over-inflates the largest
# species, so once recruitment collapses in Stage 2 the survivors pile up at that
# giant w_max (e.g. cod biomass concentrating at ~74 kg). Replace it with the
# regional biomass-weighted q99.9 survey length, which sits just above the q99
# reporting cutoff (headroom for the large fish the trawl under-catches) yet is
# robust to a single outlier tow. Herring is held at its FishBase value (its survey
# FLEN is mm-coded and it is a small forage species, not subject to the pile-up).
# R_max (an empirical *starting* value, retuned during calibration) is recomputed
# from the corrected w_max for internal consistency.
biomass_cutoffHigh_tbl <- max_weight_comparison |> select(species = species_name, biomass_cutoffHigh)
w_max_survey_tbl       <- max_weight_comparison |> select(species = species_name, w_max_survey)

external_species_info <- external_species_info |>
  select(-any_of("biomass_cutoffHigh")) |>
  left_join(biomass_cutoffHigh_tbl, by = "species") |>
  left_join(w_max_survey_tbl,       by = "species") |>
  mutate(
    w_max = ifelse(species == "Atlantic Herring" | is.na(w_max_survey),
                   w_max, round(w_max_survey, 1)),
    R_max = 10^13 * w_max^-1.5) |>
  select(-w_max_survey)

# Sanity: corrected w_max must still exceed w_mat for every species
stopifnot(all(external_species_info$w_max > external_species_info$w_mat))

```

Copy species life history parameters into the species parameters for the model
```{r}
external_species_info <-select(external_species_info,c("species","w_max","w_mat", "w_min","beta" ,"sigma" ,"a","b","age_mat","R_max" , "biomass_cutoff", "biomass_cutoffHigh"))

# Correct w_min for oviparous skates — hatchlings emerge at ~10 cm TL (~5 g),
# so w_min = 0.001 g creates phantom size classes that inflate predation mortality
# and drive erepro > 1. Verified: a * 10^b gives ~4.6 g (Winter) and ~5.6 g (Thorny).
external_species_info$w_min[external_species_info$species == "Winter Skate"] <- 5
external_species_info$w_min[external_species_info$species == "Thorny Skate"] <- 5

# ── PPMR (beta) corrections for piscivores ───────────────────────────────────
# beta values are now biomass-weighted mean PPMR from 00b_SpeciesParams_extraction.R
# (weighted.mean(ppmr, w = prey_wght)), so large fish prey dominate rather than
# numerically abundant tiny prey. No manual overrides needed.

```

REDO THIS USING DATA ABOVE:
Read in Abundance and Biomass at length from DFO RV Summer Survey (from DFO Maritimes region data team, 4VsW - see methods)
convert from KG to grams. 
Prior to calculation need to truncate the biomass at length by the same length cut_off used in the model.
Rename columns
```{r}
# Recalculate total annual biomass from raw survey data, 4VsW strata (443-466)
# Replaces pre-processed DFO_Biomass_selected_species.csv for strata consistency
biomass_obs <- stat %>%
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466,
         YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 2024) %>%
  mutate(species_name = species_code_lookup[COMMON_NAME]) %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_name)) %>%
  group_by(Year = YEAR, species_name) %>%
  summarise(biomass_g = sum(Biomass_Strata_KG, na.rm = TRUE) * 1e3, .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = species_name, values_from = biomass_g, values_fill = 0) %>%
  select(Year, any_of(species_order))
biomass_obs[is.na(biomass_obs)] <- 0

## ── FORAGE-FISH SURVEY CATCHABILITY ──────────────────────────────────────────
## The bottom-trawl survey under-represents the small pelagics for TWO distinct
## reasons, which the occurrence analysis (above) lets us separate:
##  - SIZE SELECTIVITY (a missing juvenile end): handled NOT by scaling but by the
##    occurrence-based lower cutoff + matchBiomasses over the comparable adult
##    range — mizer then ESTIMATES the unsampled small end self-consistently.
##  - WHOLE-POPULATION AVAILABILITY (off-bottom / sediment-burying): the survey
##    misses individuals of ALL sizes, so there is NO hidden size range for the
##    model to fill; this genuinely needs an explicit catchability multiplier.
## Occurrence evidence (fraction of years each 2-cm bin is caught):
##  - Atlantic Herring: adults 22-34 cm caught reliably, juveniles <16 cm missed
##    -> a real juvenile gap. We TESTED dropping the x50 (size-range matching the
##    adult window): it FAILED -- the unscaled adult target is ~50x too small for
##    herring to seed itself against web predation, so erepro -> Inf (>1) on the
##    first matchBiomasses iteration. CONCLUSION: herring's bottom-trawl deficit is
##    NOT only a juvenile size gap but also ADULT AVAILABILITY (pelagic/off-bottom)
##    -- the adult window is itself under-caught, so size-range matching can't
##    recover it. Restored to x50. The juvenile end is still extrapolated by mizer
##    below the cutoff; the x50 now stands for adult availability.
##  - Sand Lance (8-24 cm) & Capelin (10-16 cm): the survey samples nearly their
##    WHOLE size range, so under-representation is availability, not truncation ->
##    keep an explicit catchability multiplier (was x200; based approx. on
##    Harley et al. 2001 and Bundy et al.). TEST SENSITIVITY.
forage_catchability_mult <- c(
  `Atlantic Herring` = 50,   # adult availability (pelagic/off-bottom); x1 test -> erepro Inf
  `Sand Lance`       = 3000, # was 200; BOOSTED so sand lance is the dominant forage & main
                             # seal prey (Bowen 81%), letting selective seals feed on it
                             # instead of cropping herring to extinction. Sediment-burying =>
                             # survey catches a tiny fraction of true stock, so a large factor
                             # is defensible. TUNE: raise if seals still crash herring/capelin;
                             # lower if sand lance over-dominates or will not sustain.
  `Capelin`          = 200)  # availability deficit (pelagic / off-bottom)
for (sp in names(forage_catchability_mult))
  biomass_obs[[sp]] <- biomass_obs[[sp]] * forage_catchability_mult[[sp]]

```

To intialise model need to time-average biomasses between 1978 and 1985 (prior to any detectable trends in species, relatively more stable period)

```{r}
library(reshape2)
#Aggregate observed biomass to mean biomass
biomass_obs_sub <- subset(biomass_obs, Year >= 1978 & Year <= 2024)
biomass_ts <- reshape2::melt(biomass_obs_sub, id.vars = 1)
names(biomass_ts)<-c("Year","Species","Biomass")
saveRDS(biomass_ts, "Ess_data/biomass_ts.RDS") 
## Arithmetic mean
# mean_biomass_obs <- subset(biomass_ts, Year<=max(years_to_use))%>%
#   group_by(Species)%>% summarise(biomass_observed =mean(Biomass,  na.rm = T))
## Geom mean
mean_biomass_obs <- subset(biomass_ts, Year <= max(years_to_use)) %>%
  group_by(Species) %>% summarise( biomass_observed = exp(mean(log(Biomass[Biomass > 0]), na.rm = TRUE)))

mean_biomass_obs$biomass_observed<- ifelse(is.nan( mean_biomass_obs$biomass_observed),NA,  mean_biomass_obs$biomass_observed)

```

Set up fishing gear parameters
```{r}
fishing_type <- read.csv("Ess_data/new.gear_params.csv")
names(fishing_type)[1] <- "species"

new_seal <- read.csv("Ess_data/seal_gear_params.csv")

#new_seal$catchability <- new_seal$catchability / 10   # Reduce initial seal catchability

# Gaussian size-selectivity function (used by mizer internally)
gaussian_sizeweight <- function(w, species_params, w_opt, sigma, ...) {
  exp(-0.5 * ((log(w) - log(w_opt)) / sigma)^2)
}

rownames(fishing_type) <- paste(fishing_type$species, fishing_type$gear, sep = ", ")
rownames(new_seal)     <- paste(new_seal$species,     new_seal$gear,     sep = ", ")
updated_gp <- bind_rows(fishing_type, new_seal)

```

Include  more realistic interaction matrix: 
no predation on Alt. Halibut
guild feeding based on Cook & Bundy DFO report

```{r interaction-matrix}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4VsW MULTISPECIES INTERACTION MATRIX
# Schoener's D spatial overlap used directly as θ_ij (habitat encounter prob.)
# Strata 443–466 | 19 species | Cook & Bundy 2010
# Strata 440–442 are NAFO 4Vn (northeastern shelf) — excluded.
# Stratum 443 confirmed as 4Vs — included.
# Strata 434–439 are inshore/edge (very low biomass) — excluded.
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

library(tidyverse)
library(factoextra)

# ── 1. STRATA VERIFICATION ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stat$strat_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(stat$STRAT)))

strat_biomass <- aggregate(Biomass_Strata_KG ~ strat_num,
                           data = stat[!is.na(stat$strat_num), ], sum, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Strata included (443-466, 4VsW domain) and their total biomass (kg):\n")
print(strat_biomass[strat_biomass$strat_num >= 443 & strat_biomass$strat_num <= 466, ])
cat("\nExcluded strata 440-442 (NAFO 4Vn — northeastern shelf, outside model domain):\n")
print(strat_biomass[strat_biomass$strat_num %in% 440:442, ])

# ── 2. NAME MAP: raw survey name → model species name ────────────────────────
name_map <- c(
  "COD(ATLANTIC)"              = "Atlantic Cod",
  "HADDOCK"                    = "Haddock",
  "REDFISH UNSEPARATED"        = "Redfish Unseparated",
  "AMERICAN PLAICE"            = "American Plaice",
  "SILVER HAKE"                = "Silver Hake",
  "MONKFISH,GOOSEFISH,ANGLER"  = "Monkfish",
  "WHITE HAKE"                 = "White Hake",
  "THORNY SKATE"               = "Thorny Skate",
  "WINTER SKATE"               = "Winter Skate",
  "POLLOCK"                    = "Pollock",
  "YELLOWTAIL FLOUNDER"        = "Yellowtail Flounder",
  "LONGHORN SCULPIN"           = "Longhorn Sculpin",
  "SQUIRREL OR RED HAKE"       = "Red Hake",
  "HERRING(ATLANTIC)"          = "Atlantic Herring",
  "NORTHERN SAND LANCE"        = "Sand Lance",
  "SPINY DOGFISH"              = "Spiny Dogfish",
  "HALIBUT(ATLANTIC)"          = "Atlantic Halibut",
  "CAPELIN"                    = "Capelin",
  "WITCH FLOUNDER"             = "Witch Flounder"
)

# ── 3. BUILD STRATUM × SPECIES BIOMASS MATRIX ────────────────────────────────
stratum_matrix <- stat %>%
  filter(COMMON_NAME %in% names(name_map)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466) %>%
  group_by(strat_num, COMMON_NAME) %>%
  summarise(biomass = sum(Biomass_Strata_KG, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = COMMON_NAME, values_from = biomass, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("strat_num")

# Check all 19 species present
missing_spp <- setdiff(names(name_map), colnames(stratum_matrix))
if (length(missing_spp) > 0) warning("Missing from stratum matrix: ", paste(missing_spp, collapse = ", "))

# ── 4. SCHOENER'S D ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
col_sums <- colSums(stratum_matrix)
col_sums[col_sums == 0] <- 1
dist_norm      <- sweep(stratum_matrix, 2, col_sums, "/")
schoener_raw   <- 1 - (as.matrix(dist(t(dist_norm), method = "manhattan")) / 2)
diag(schoener_raw) <- 0.2

# Map to model names and reorder to match params species order
colnames(schoener_raw) <- name_map[colnames(schoener_raw)]
rownames(schoener_raw) <- name_map[rownames(schoener_raw)]
sp_order     <- species_params(params)$species
schoener_D   <- schoener_raw[sp_order, sp_order]

cat("\nSchoener's D matrix (strata 440-466):\n")
print(round(schoener_D, 2))

# ── 5. CLUSTERING & DENDROGRAM ───────────────────────────────────────────────
d   <- as.dist(1 - schoener_D)
fit <- hclust(d, method = "ward.D2")

plot(fit,
     main = "4VsW Species Co-occurrence (Strata 443-466)",
     sub  = "Schoener's D | Ward.D2",
     xlab = "", ylab = "Ecological distance", hang = -1)
abline(h = 0.5, col = "red", lty = 2)
rect.hclust(fit, h = 0.5, border = "blue")

fviz_dend(fit, h = 0.5, type = "rectangle", rect = TRUE, rect_fill = TRUE,
          k_colors = "jco", cex = 0.6,
          main = "4VsW Ecological Guilds — Strata 443-466")

clusters <- cutree(fit, h = 0.5)
cat("\nGuild assignments (h = 0.5):\n")
print(sort(clusters))

# ── 6. INTERACTION MATRIX — scaled Schoener's D (4VsW depth-stratum overlap) ─
# θ_ij in mizer scales encounter rates between predator i and prey j.
# Schoener's D is ecologically appropriate here: it measures spatial co-occurrence
# (i.e. whether species share habitat and can encounter each other), which is
# the correct biological basis for θ_ij — diet composition (Cook & Bundy) captures
# what is eaten after an encounter, which is already handled by the feeding kernel.
# Raw D values (0.4–0.9) cause predation overload when used directly; scaling by
# 0.3 brings co-occurring pairs to θ ~0.12–0.27 while preserving 4VsW structure.
# Diagonal (intraspecific) set to 0.3 independently.
inter <- schoener_D * 0.3
diag(inter) <- 0.3

# Elasmobranchs rarely consumed — defended by spines/size; scale down as prey
inter[, "Spiny Dogfish"]  <- inter[, "Spiny Dogfish"]  * 0.3
inter[, "Thorny Skate"]   <- inter[, "Thorny Skate"]   * 0.5
inter[, "Winter Skate"]   <- inter[, "Winter Skate"]   * 0.5

# ── Cook & Bundy column overrides (diet data > spatial overlap for these prey) ─

# Sand Lance: dominant prey for flatfish & Haddock in C&B but beta too high for
# their feeding kernel to reach sand lance size — boost column to compensate
inter["Haddock",             "Sand Lance"] <- 0.60
inter["American Plaice",     "Sand Lance"] <- 0.70
inter["Yellowtail Flounder", "Sand Lance"] <- 0.70
inter["Witch Flounder",      "Sand Lance"] <- 0.40
inter["Longhorn Sculpin",    "Sand Lance"] <- 0.50
inter["Atlantic Cod",        "Sand Lance"] <- 0.50
inter["Thorny Skate",        "Sand Lance"] <- 0.60
inter["Winter Skate",        "Sand Lance"] <- 0.40

# Atlantic Herring: C&B dominant prey for true piscivores only
# White Hake 34.46%, Cod 18.31%, Pollock/Dogfish/Monkfish heuristic
inter["White Hake",      "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.60
inter["Spiny Dogfish",   "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.50
inter["Pollock",         "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.55
inter["Monkfish",        "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.50
inter["Atlantic Cod",    "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.60

# Invertivores: C&B shows Herring is negligible — cap low so Schoener's D
# base value doesn't inflate Herring predation for these species
# Haddock 0.07%, American Plaice 0%, Yellowtail Flounder 0.05%,
# Witch Flounder ~0%, Longhorn Sculpin ~0%
inter["Haddock",             "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["American Plaice",     "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["Yellowtail Flounder", "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["Witch Flounder",      "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["Longhorn Sculpin",    "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05

# American Plaice: model over-predates; C&B shows mainly Thorny Skate eating it
inter[, "American Plaice"] <- inter[, "American Plaice"] * 0.3
inter["Thorny Skate", "American Plaice"] <- 0.50   # restore Thorny Skate (C&B dominant)

# Forage fish do not eat each other — zero out Herring↔Capelin cross-predation
inter["Atlantic Herring", "Capelin"]     <- 0.0
inter["Capelin",          "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.0

params <- setInteraction(params, interaction = inter)

cat("\nInteraction matrix (scaled Schoener's D × 0.3):\n")
print(round(interaction_matrix(params), 2))
```

Set up functions to exclude Seal from Yield plots

```{r}

fishing_gears <- c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic")

# Wrapper: exclude specified gears (default "Seals") from model yield before comparing to
# observed NAFO catches. Seals are parameterised as a gear but represent external predation,
# not commercial catch — including them inflates modelled yield per species.
plotYieldExcl <- function(params, exclude_gear = "Seals", ...) {
  gp <- gear_params(params)
  gear_params(params) <- gp[!gp$gear %in% exclude_gear, ]
  plotYieldObservedVsModel(params, ...)
}

# Wrapper: exclude Seals gear from Fmort plot. Seals are added as a gear for
# convenience but their mortality is predation, not fishing — including them
# conflates fishing F with predation M in the diagnostic plot.
plotFMortExcl <- function(params, exclude_gear = "Seals", ...) {
  gp <- gear_params(params)
  gear_params(params) <- gp[!gp$gear %in% exclude_gear, ]
  plotlyFMort(params, ...)
}

# Plot comparison of model-predicted vs observed biomass
# - ratio = TRUE: plots the ratio (model / observed), ideal value is 1
# - labels = FALSE: do not display species names on the plot
plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params, ratio = TRUE, labels = FALSE)

# Plot comparison of model-predicted vs observed yield (catch) — seals excluded
# - ratio = TRUE: shows how well the model predicts catch relative to observed data
# - labels = FALSE: cleaner plot without species labels
plotYieldExcl(params, ratio = TRUE, labels = FALSE)

# Plot interactive feeding level by size for each species
# Shows how close species are to satiation (values near 1 = full, <0.2 = hungry)
# Useful to check realism of trophic dynamics and possible starvation
plotlyFeedingLevel(params)
```      

# STEP 3: Set Sensitivity to Fishing

Set up how model responses to fishing - resilience to fishing is influenced by the reproduction paramters being estimated by the steps above....

- need to  check Fvsyield curves(and other plots)
```{r include = FALSE}

# reproduction_level = RDD / R_max (density dependence of recruitment).
#  - HIGHER rl (→1): recruitment strongly buffered (near R_max), insensitive to
#    spawner biomass → MORE resilient, dome-shaped yield-vs-F peaking at HIGHER F,
#    and a finite (small) R_max.
#  - LOWER rl (→0): recruitment ∝ egg production, little compensation → stock
#    collapses/recovers in step with spawners, dome peaks at LOWER F, and
#    R_max → ∞ (donor-controlled — the instability to avoid).
# Set per-species by life-history resilience; floor the low-fecundity species at
# ~0.3-0.4 so R_max stays finite. Verify each against the plotYieldVsF panel below
# (dome should peak near the stock's single-species Fmsy).
rl_vec <- c(
  "Atlantic Cod"        = 0.45,  # lower → reinforces seal-driven non-recovery
  "Haddock"             = 0.60,
  "Pollock"             = 0.55,
  "Silver Hake"         = 0.60,
  "White Hake"          = 0.50,
  "Red Hake"            = 0.60,
  "American Plaice"     = 0.50,
  "Yellowtail Flounder" = 0.50,
  "Witch Flounder"      = 0.50,
  "Longhorn Sculpin"    = 0.65,
  "Atlantic Herring"    = 0.65,  # high-fecundity forage → strong compensation
  "Sand Lance"          = 0.65,
  "Capelin"             = 0.65,
  "Redfish Unseparated" = 0.40,  # viviparous, very slow
  "Monkfish"            = 0.40,
  "Thorny Skate"        = 0.35,  # K-strategists: low but FINITE (avoid Inf R_max)
  "Winter Skate"        = 0.35,
  "Spiny Dogfish"       = 0.35,  # ~6 pups / 2-yr gestation — almost no compensation
  "Atlantic Halibut"    = 0.45
)
params <- setBevertonHolt(params,
            reproduction_level = rl_vec[species_params(params)$species])
```

# STEP 4: 
## CHECK SEAL CATCHABILITY TUNING
```{r}
# ── SEAL CATCHABILITY TUNING ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Run AFTER initial matchBiomasses loop, BEFORE matchYield
seal_abundance   <- readRDS("Ess_data/seal_abundance_digitised.RDS")
ref_years        <- 1978:1985
ref_n_seals      <- mean(seal_abundance$scotian_mean[seal_abundance$year %in% ref_years]) * 1000

seal_body_mass_g       <- 170 * 1000    # confirmed: Bundy 2004 Scotian Shelf EwE
total_biomass_g        <- ref_n_seals * seal_body_mass_g
QB_seal                <- 12.98         # confirmed: Bundy 2004 Table A (Q/B for grey seals)
fish_fraction          <- 0.85          # confirmed: Bowen et al. 1993; DFO grey seal diet
Yield_observed_seals_g <- total_biomass_g * QB_seal * fish_fraction

seal_gear_name <- "Seals"

get_seal_yield <- function(p) {
  sum(sapply(species_params(p)$species, function(sp) {
    n <- initialN(p)[sp, ]
    f <- getFMortGear(p)[seal_gear_name, sp, ]
    sum(f * n * p@w * p@dw)
  }), na.rm = TRUE)
}

# SEALS OFF during the steady-state calibration — Q/B scaling DEFERRED to after
# the biomass loops (post-hoc; see 00e_digitise_seal_data.r note). Running the
# empirical (juvenile-focused) seal gear during matchBiomasses drives
# reproduction_level -> 0 (R_max -> Inf) for the low-productivity species and
# distorts the 1978-85 reference state (cod dynamics flip). We keep the target
# (Yield_observed_seals_g) and the empirical catchabilities for the post-hoc step.
seal_rows <- which(gear_params(params)$gear == seal_gear_name)
seal_gp_species <- gear_params(params)$species[seal_rows]
seal_catchability_init <- new_seal$catchability[match(seal_gp_species, new_seal$species)]
gear_params(params)$catchability[seal_rows] <- 0   # seals OFF for calibration
params <- steady(params)
cat("Seals OFF for steady-state calibration; Q/B scaling deferred to post-hoc step.\n")


```


-Check ratio between modelled and obs catches, rescale catchability
-Adjust catchability, then setady state again

```{r}

## Second calibration pass (after reproduction_level set + seals turned OFF):
## biomass + yield only. matchGrowth is deliberately NOT used (see note below).
#fishing_gears <- c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic")

# ── STEP 5: biomass + yield re-calibration with seals OFF (NO matchGrowth) ────
# matchGrowth (gamma/search-volume adjustment) DESTABILISES this loop once the
# corrected empirical seal gear imposes juvenile predation on the low-productivity
# species (skates, monkfish, white hake): it drives their recruitment (RDI) to 0,
# erepro blows up (1e11-1e20), and setBevertonHolt errors "no reproduction".
# Per the digitise-script intent, GROWTH IS HANDLED SEPARATELY — this step only
# gets the biomasses into the right ballpark (matchBiomasses) with catchabilities
# (matchYield). Growth is checked in the diagnostic below and, if von Bertalanffy
# fit is poor, tuned as a one-off (matchGrowth on the final stable params, or
# manual gamma) AFTER this loop — not interleaved with it.
 for (i in 1:20) {
   params <- params |>
     matchYield(keep = "biomass", gears = fishing_gears) |> steady() |>
     matchBiomasses() |> steady()
 }
 params_my <- params   # diagnostics reflect the calibrated result (not pre-loop)

 plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params_my, ratio = TRUE)
 plotGrowthCurves(params_my, species_panel = TRUE)   # growth check — handled separately
 plotYieldExcl(params_my, ratio = TRUE)
 plotFMortExcl(params_my)

# # ── STEP 5b: check reproduction_level via yield-vs-F curves ──────────────────
# # Run BEFORE matchYield: catchabilities should be set on a model with the
# # correct stock-recruitment shape. reproduction_level = 0.7 set earlier.
# # Yield curves should be dome-shaped peaking at realistic F (~0.2–0.5).
# # If any species is flat (rl too low) or collapses at very low F (rl too high),
# # adjust here then re-run steady() before proceeding.
# plotYieldVsF(params,species="Spiny Dogfish")
# 
# # Example overrides if needed (uncomment and re-run steady):
#  rep_tuned <- getReproductionLevel(params_my)
#  rep_tuned[] <- 0.5
#  params <- setBevertonHolt(params, reproduction_level = rep_tuned) |> steady()

params_steady <- params
```


## STEP 6: final biomass match + POST-HOC seal Q/B calibration
```{r seal-catchability-calibration}

# final matchBiomass (still seals-off → clean fishing-only steady state)
for (i in 1:6) {
params_steady <- params_steady |> matchBiomasses() |> steady()
}
cat("Inf R_max before seals:", sum(is.infinite(species_params(params_steady)$R_max)), "\n")

# ── POST-HOC SEAL Q/B CALIBRATION ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fishing-only steady state is now set (finite R_max, growth, biomass). Add the
# empirical seal gear and scale its catchabilities to the Q/B consumption target,
# as a perturbation on the stable state (NOT followed by matchBiomasses, which
# would re-trigger the R_max->Inf cascade). At the 1978-85 reference seal effort
# this is a modest perturbation; the large seal predation ramps in Stage 2.
seal_rows <- which(gear_params(params_steady)$gear == seal_gear_name)
gear_params(params_steady)$catchability[seal_rows] <- seal_catchability_init
params_steady <- steady(params_steady)
scale_factor_seal <- Yield_observed_seals_g / get_seal_yield(params_steady)
gear_params(params_steady)$catchability[seal_rows] <-
  gear_params(params_steady)$catchability[seal_rows] * scale_factor_seal
params_steady <- steady(params_steady)
cat("Post-hoc seal Q/B — model/target ratio:",
    round(get_seal_yield(params_steady) / Yield_observed_seals_g, 3), "\n")
cat("Inf R_max after seals: ", sum(is.infinite(species_params(params_steady)$R_max)), "\n")

# ── DIAGNOSTIC: model-estimated population BELOW the survey cutoff ────────────
# matchBiomasses fitted the model to the survey within each species' [low, high]
# size window; mizer's spectrum estimates the unsampled small end below the lower
# cutoff. For the forage fish this below-cutoff biomass is the "remaining part of
# the population" the survey can't see (e.g. herring juveniles <16 cm) — sanity-
# check it's plausible, not exploding. Integrate initial_n like matchBiomassesCustom.
spp_steady <- species_params(params_steady)
w_g  <- params_steady@w
dw_g <- params_steady@dw
small_end <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(spp_steady)), function(sp) {
  low  <- spp_steady$biomass_cutoff[sp];     if (is.na(low))  low  <- 0
  high <- spp_steady$biomass_cutoffHigh[sp]; if (is.na(high)) high <- Inf
  n    <- params_steady@initial_n[sp, ]
  B_window <- sum(n[w_g >= low & w_g <= high] * w_g[w_g >= low & w_g <= high] *
                    dw_g[w_g >= low & w_g <= high])      # matched to survey
  B_below  <- sum(n[w_g <  low] * w_g[w_g <  low] * dw_g[w_g <  low]) # estimated small end
  data.frame(species = spp_steady$species[sp], cutoff_g = round(low, 1),
             B_window_g = signif(B_window, 3), B_below_g = signif(B_below, 3),
             pct_below = round(100 * B_below / (B_window + B_below), 1))
}))
cat("\nModel-estimated biomass below vs within the survey size window (forage fish):\n")
print(small_end[small_end$species %in%
        c("Atlantic Herring","Sand Lance","Capelin"), ], row.names = FALSE)

plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)
plotYieldExcl(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)


plotFMortExcl(params_steady)

# ── SEAL PREDATION MORTALITY PER SPECIES ─────────────────────────────────────
# Seals are a gear so their mortality appears in getFMortGear, not getM2.
# Compute biomass-weighted mean seal-F per species as a proxy for predation pressure.
# Compare against total M2 (fish predation mortality) to judge relative importance.
seal_fmort_mat <- getFMortGear(params_steady)[seal_gear_name, , ]
biomass_mat    <- sweep(initialN(params_steady), 2, params_steady@w * params_steady@dw, "*")
seal_f_mean    <- rowSums(seal_fmort_mat * biomass_mat) / rowSums(biomass_mat)

m2_mat         <- getM2(params_steady)
m2_mean        <- rowSums(m2_mat * biomass_mat) / rowSums(biomass_mat)

seal_mortality_summary <- data.frame(
  species     = names(seal_f_mean),
  seal_F_mean = round(seal_f_mean, 4),
  M2_mean     = round(m2_mean, 4),
  seal_pct_M2 = round(100 * seal_f_mean / (m2_mean + 1e-10), 1)
) |> arrange(desc(seal_F_mean))

print(seal_mortality_summary)

# Check per-species seal consumption
plotYieldGear(projectToSteady(params_steady, return_sim = TRUE), gears = "Seals")
totalQSeals <- sum(getYieldGear(projectToSteady(params_steady, return_sim = TRUE))[2,"Seals",])


```


## Diagnostics: Now check steady state, again
```{r}

# Run the model to steady state and return the full simulation object
# - return_sim = TRUE: keeps the time series data (vs. just returning final params)
# - t_max = 100: allows up to 100 time steps to reach convergence
sim <- steady(params_steady, return_sim = TRUE, t_max = 100)
# Quick plot of total biomass and yields over time (main summary)
plot(sim)

# Check Diagnostic plots
# Plot species biomass over time
# Useful to check if species stabilize or fluctuate at steady state
plotBiomass(sim)

# Plot spectra (biomass by size) from the final state
# Reveals trophic structure and size-based energy flow
plotSpectra(sim)

# Plot species diet composition by size
# Shows who eats whom across size classes
plotDiet(params_steady)

# Plot growth curves for each species
# - species_panel = TRUE: shows separate panels per species
# - max_age = 20: restricts plots to ages up to 20
plotGrowthCurves(params_steady, species_panel = TRUE, max_age = 20)

# Compare model vs observed yield (catch) — seals excluded from model yield
# - ratio = TRUE: visualizes model/observed ratio; ideal = 1
plotYieldExcl(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)

# Compare model vs observed biomass
# - ratio = TRUE: visualizes model/observed ratio; ideal = 1
plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)

# Plot feeding level by size
# Reveals how full each species is at each size (0 = starving, 1 = satiated)
plotFeedingLevel(params_steady)
```

```{r diet-validation-cb}
# Normalise C&B within each predator so fish-prey proportions sum to 1
cb_norm <- cb_raw %>%
  group_by(Predator) %>%
  mutate(cb_prop = pct / sum(pct)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Predator, Prey, cb_prop, source)

# `diet` from the chunk above: Predator, Prey, Ratio (model fish-prey proportions)
diet_compare <- diet %>%
  rename(model_prop = Ratio) %>%
  full_join(cb_norm, by = c("Predator", "Prey")) %>%
  filter(cb_prop > 0.01 | model_prop > 0.01) %>%  # drop negligible entries
  mutate(
    model_prop = replace_na(model_prop, 0),
    cb_prop    = replace_na(cb_prop, 0)
  )



# ── Heatmap: model diet proportions alongside C&B (side-by-side) ─────────
diet_long <- diet_compare %>%
  pivot_longer(c(model_prop, cb_prop),
               names_to = "type", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(type = recode(type,
                       model_prop = "Model (mizer)",
                       cb_prop    = "Cook & Bundy"))

ggplot(diet_long, aes(x = Prey, y = Predator, fill = prop)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~type) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
                       name = "Fish-prey\nproportion") +
  labs(title = "Diet comparison: mizer vs Cook & Bundy (2010)",
       x = "Prey", y = "Predator") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 7),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 7),
        strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid   = element_blank())
```

Create size spectrum plots by species with size distribution data from DFO RV Trawl Surveys (q-corrected)

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Reshape biomass-at-length to long format (4VsW strata 443-466)
bio_size <- stat |>
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) |>
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466) |>
  filter(YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 1985) |>
  select(Year = YEAR,species_name_raw = COMMON_NAME,
    length_cm = FLEN, Biomass = Biomass_Strata_KG) |>
  mutate(# Herring FLEN is recorded in mm (all rows) — convert to cm to match other species
    length_cm = ifelse(species_name_raw == "HERRING(ATLANTIC)", length_cm / 10, length_cm),
    Species = species_code_lookup[species_name_raw]) |>
  filter(!is.na(Species)) |> select(Year, Species, length_cm, Biomass)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Check observed length range per species
# ------------------------------------------------------------
max_min_size <- bio_size |>
  group_by(Species) |>
  summarise(min_l = min(length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),max_l = max(length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")

print(max_min_size)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Join L-W parameters and compute weight
# ------------------------------------------------------------
wl <- data.frame(Species = species_params(params)$species,
                 a = species_params(params)$a,b = species_params(params)$b)

bio_size <- bio_size |> left_join(wl, by = "Species") |>
  mutate(  w = a * length_cm ^ b) |> filter(!is.na(Biomass), !is.na(w),w > 0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Bin into weight classes and normalise biomass
# ------------------------------------------------------------
breaks <- 10 ^ seq(0, 6, 0.5)
low    <- head(breaks, -1)
upp    <- tail(breaks, -1)
widths <- upp - low
mid    <- (low + upp) / 2

bio_size <- bio_size |> mutate(bin_id = as.integer(cut(w, breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)),
    weightclass = mid[bin_id],norm_biomass = Biomass / widths[bin_id]) |>
  filter( !is.na(weightclass),!is.na(norm_biomass),is.finite(norm_biomass))

write.csv(bio_size, "Ess_data/bio_size.csv", row.names = FALSE)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Summarise: normalised biomass per weight class x year x species
# ------------------------------------------------------------
biomass_size_spectra <- bio_size |> group_by(weightclass, Year, Species) |>
  summarise(nbiomass = sum(norm_biomass, na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop" )

mean_biomass_size_spectra <- biomass_size_spectra |>
  group_by(weightclass, Species) |>
  summarise( mean_nbiomass = mean(nbiomass, na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot: mizer spectra + observed biomass size spectra
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Biomass cutoff lines
# ------------------------------------------------------------
cutoff_lines <- external_species_info |>
  select(Species = species,biomass_cutoff) |> filter(!is.na(biomass_cutoff))

size_distributions <- plotSpectra( params_steady,power = 0,resource = FALSE) +

  # observed spectra
  geom_point(data = mean_biomass_size_spectra,
    aes( x = weightclass,y = mean_nbiomass, colour = Species),inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # biomass cutoff thresholds
  geom_vline(
    data = cutoff_lines, aes(xintercept = biomass_cutoff),
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7,colour = "black",inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Weight class (g)",y = "Normalised mean biomass")+
    #title = "Observed biomass-at-size compared with mizer spectra",
    #subtitle = "Dashed lines indicate biomass cutoff thresholds") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) )

size_distributions
ggsave(filename = paste0(save_dir, "size_distributions.jpeg"), plot = size_distributions,
       width = 10, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)
```

```{r}
    aspect.ratio    = 0.8)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Yield plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------
Calibration_pb_yield <- plotYieldExcl(params, ratio = FALSE, labels = FALSE, return_data = TRUE)

pb_yield <- mean(1 - Calibration_pb_yield$ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

Calibration_plot_Y <- ggplot(
  Calibration_pb_yield,
  aes(x = species, y = 1 - ratio, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.1) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf,label = expression(bold("(c)")),
  parse = TRUE, size = 3, hjust = 21.5, vjust = 2.1) +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "1 - Modelled/Observed") +
  calibration_theme

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Biomass plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------
Calibration_pb_biomass <- plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params, ratio = FALSE, labels = FALSE, return_data = TRUE)

pb_biomass <- mean(1 - Calibration_pb_biomass$ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

Calibration_plot_B <- ggplot(
  Calibration_pb_biomass,
  aes(x = species, y = 1 - ratio, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.1) +
  annotate("text",
    x     = length(unique(Calibration_pb_biomass$species)) + 0.5,
    y     = max(1 - Calibration_pb_biomass$ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    label = expression(bold("(d)")),
    parse = TRUE, size = 3, hjust = 20.5, vjust = 1.1) +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "1 - Modelled/Observed") +
  calibration_theme

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Combined plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------
Calibration_plot <- combined_plot / (Calibration_plot_Y + Calibration_plot_B)
Calibration_plot
ggsave(filename = paste0(save_dir, "Calibration_plot.jpeg"), plot = Calibration_plot,
       width = 11,height = 8.5, units = "in",dpi = 400)

Calibration_plot
```



## STAGE 1 DIAGNOSTIC — emergent seal "catch" composition vs Bowen & Harrison (1994)

Compare the model's emergent seal diet (consumption by species, % wet weight) at the
steady state to the observed offshore grey-seal diet (Bowen & Harrison 1994, Table 2).
Bowen is a single high-sand-lance-year snapshot, so this is an informal check on whether
the seal gear apportions consumption sensibly given the model's prey field — not a target.

```{r seal-diet-vs-bowen}
# Emergent seal consumption per species at the steady state
seal_F <- getFMortGear(params_steady)["Seals", , ]   # [species x size]
n_ss   <- initialN(params_steady)                     # [species x size]
ww     <- params_steady@w * params_steady@dw          # weight x bin-width
w_mat  <- matrix(ww, nrow = nrow(n_ss), ncol = length(ww), byrow = TRUE)
cons_g <- rowSums(seal_F * n_ss * w_mat)              # consumption (g) per species
seal_diet <- data.frame(
  species   = species_params(params_steady)$species,
  model_pct = round(100 * cons_g / sum(cons_g), 1)
)

# Bowen & Harrison (1994) Table 2, % wet weight (offshore Sable Island)
bowen <- c("Sand Lance"=80.9, "Atlantic Cod"=11.0, "Silver Hake"=2.6,
           "American Plaice"=1.4, "Redfish Unseparated"=1.3,
           "Yellowtail Flounder"=1.1, "Witch Flounder"=0.4, "Capelin"=0.4,
           "Pollock"=0.2, "White Hake"=0.2, "Atlantic Herring"=0.2, "Haddock"=0.05)
seal_diet$bowen_pct <- ifelse(seal_diet$species %in% names(bowen),
                              bowen[seal_diet$species], 0)

seal_diet <- seal_diet[order(-seal_diet$model_pct), ]
print(seal_diet)

# Side-by-side heatmap (model vs Bowen)
seal_long <- seal_diet %>%
  pivot_longer(c(model_pct, bowen_pct), names_to = "source", values_to = "pct") %>%
  mutate(source = recode(source, model_pct = "Model (emergent)",
                         bowen_pct = "Bowen & Harrison 1994"))
ggplot(seal_long, aes(x = source, y = reorder(species, pct), fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1, name = "% diet") +
  labs(title = "Grey seal diet: model emergent vs Bowen & Harrison (1994)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)

```
